warning_yard.name: Warning Yard
warning_yard.description: NOT A HAZARD — a picture of one. A 7.5 m plot of ground with a 3.0 m pit cut clean through it, 1.20 m deep, a broken lip, a gate on the far edge and a worn track from the gate to the hole. The pit, the gate and the track are byte-identical at every value of the axis; only the MARKING changes. none leaves it unmarked. stain soaks the yard with the evidence of past harm and two drag runs toward the gate. cage fences it at 2.30 m with a kick board and three filed tags. beacon stands a lighting mast at the far corner and burns a lit rim round the lip. shroud pulls a canvas over the whole opening so the ground reads continuous. There is no CollisionShape3D, no StaticBody3D, no Area3D, no DangerZone and no damage anywhere in this artifact at any value: it is built entirely from MeshInstance3D and it will not hurt anybody. If you place it expecting a trap you will get a picture of one.
warning_yard.safety: INERT BY CONSTRUCTION AND ON PURPOSE. Zero colliders, zero areas, zero bodies, zero lights, zero groups that any hazard or combat system reads, zero damage numbers, and no `h:` utility code is implied or required. The only group used is `hazard_warning`, which is the family's own private handle for finding the dressing again to take it down, and which nothing outside commons/hazards reads (checked across the tree). A player can walk through the plate and through the pit as if neither were there, because neither is: this is a diorama of a marked hazard and the whole argument is about the MARKING, not about the danger. Do not add a DangerZone to make it real — a marking that is backed by a working trap stops being a picture of how markings work and becomes one more hazard.
interactions: stand at the gate and ask whether the marking reached you there
compare the five markings on one unchanged pit
at shroud, look for the hole and notice the ground reads continuous
warning_yard.capacity: SEE that `warning` is not a scale from quiet to loud. Four of its five values address a person who is about to walk in — the ground under their feet, their body at the fence, their eye at the gate — and one addresses a person who would rather not look at it. The pit is the same pit at all five.
warning_yard.qfep_connection: F is the pit: one opening, one depth, one broken lip, evaluated once at build time and identical in every frame, which is what makes the row a comparison rather than five drawings. E is the five markings, and they are irreducible to one another — you cannot recover a stain from a beacon or a cage from a shroud, because they are answers to different questions about who is being protected. lambda is how much of what is here the yard is willing to say out loud. The dark spot is `shroud`, which is the only value that reduces what a visitor can know and the only one that makes the yard photograph as safe; a system that measures markings by how much calm they produce would rank it first.
warning_yard.relationships:
Synthesised from the ten registry tokens that declare a `warning` axis, all of which were read — code, registry entry, note, still_note and declines.

[[path_block]] is the source this yard preloads. One scene serves three of the family's ten tokens ([[path_cube]], [[path_wedge]], [[path_pyramid]]), its whole body is the warning apparatus with nothing else in it, and it preloads a single shader — so WARNING_VALUES and all eight WARN_* colours are read out of its file at runtime rather than retyped here. Its five paragraphs of axis doc are the yard's brief: 'the warning exists but it is addressed to your feet', 'a world that DOCUMENTS its obstacles has not removed any', 'the verdict is broadcast as light, readable across a dark room before you commit to walking', 'the quietest tile and the loudest claim'.

[[kaleidocycle_enemy]] is where the five builders and the `hazard_warning` group were first written, and every later member says so. Its construction — dressing appended LAST so nothing built above it moves an index, an unrecognised word keeping the standing value — is reproduced here for the same reasons.

[[cube_projectile_spawner]] contributes the family's sharpest self-criticism, in its own registry note: the spawner is not the danger, it is the SOURCE of the danger, so what a room says about a currently idle box is not a property of the box. This yard is the same observation one step further out — the marking is not a property of the pit at all, and the pit does not change when it is relabelled.

[[kresling_spire]] is the family's sniper, 'the only member that never reaches you, so the only warning it could ever give is what it looks like from across the room'. That sentence is why this artifact has a gate 3.35 m from the pit's centre — 1.85 m of open ground from the lip — and a worn track of exactly that length between them: the family keeps reasoning about a doorway and a distance, and not one of its ten members contains either.

[[miura_crawler]], [[scissor_stalker]] and [[origami_droideka]] are the three folding foes that carry the vocabulary unchanged; the droideka is a finding rather than a source (see dna.kin).

[[force_vortex]] carries the word on something that is not a body at all, which is the strongest evidence in the family that `warning` is about the room's speech and not the creature's anatomy.

[[r_c]] is the dissenter, and it is worth more to this yard than any of the conformists: four values, reordered, `shroud` absent, and a default of `beacon` rather than `none`. Its notes say why — at a resting pose beacon and none are identical by construction, 'which is the axis's own point, not a harness fault'. See dna.kin for what its short list costs.

Structurally this follows [[retention_corridor]] and [[evidence_ladder]]: one phenomenon solved ONCE at build time and read N ways, so nothing on the bench can disagree with anything else on it. It replaces no member. Meeting one hazard wearing one marking in a walked room is the curriculum; this is the plot where the comparison can be made.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: 7.5 m square at the plate, so it needs an 8 x 8 clear patch. The gate is on the -Z edge and the artifact reads correctly only if the approach is from that side; `orientation: face_approach` plus a rotation in the map token is how you get that. Nothing here is a collider, so the pathfinder will route straight across the pit — which is correct, because there is no pit, there is a picture of one.

measurements.measured_by: computed from the script's own layout constants, not from a capture — no Godot was run, per the brief. MeshInstance3D only, which is what the capture AABB counts, and every mesh in this artifact is a MeshInstance3D so the mesh extent IS the body. X and Z are YARD_HALF * 2 = 7.50. Y runs from 0 (the plate underside, so the grid's base-to-floor grounding is a no-op and no auto_ground opt-out is needed) to 3.89 = GROUND_TOP 1.30 + mast 2.10 + cap offset 0.445 + half the cap's 0.09 thickness. That top is the `beacon` value's cap; the default `shroud` alone tops out at 2.049, and the sweep's union box is the one framing was derived from.

dna.default:
warning=shroud. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is nothing to preserve and the default is a free design choice; the rule that outranks everything in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md is about promotions of placed artifacts and has no work to do here. That freedom was used for the strongest single reading rather than the emptiest, and `none` — which nine of the ten family members ship as their default — is exactly the emptiest.

WHY SHROUD AND NOT CAGE OR NONE. Three reasons, in order of weight. (1) It is the only value that can be inferred FROM: a taut canvas with straps and four skirts standing on a plot of ground says there is something under it, so a visitor who meets only the default still meets the axis. A visitor who meets `none` meets a hole in the ground and no question at all. (2) It is the value no member of the family can photograph. On a 1 m block a shroud is a lump you cannot identify — path_block's own doc says so: 'you cannot tell wall from ramp until you touch it'. On a plot of ground it is a low pale mound in an otherwise flat yard, the opening is gone from the picture entirely, and the ground reads CONTINUOUS from the gate, which is to say walkable. That is a different and stronger claim, and it only exists at this scale, which is the entire justification for building the yard. (3) It is the value the brief names as the argument: four of these protect a person and one protects a sensibility.

THE OBJECTION, ANSWERED. At `shroud` the pit is invisible, so a default tile does not show the hazard — the artifact could read as an empty yard with a tarp in it. It does not, and the geometry is what stops it: the crown stands 0.66 m proud of a dead-flat plate, four skirts fall to the ground on all sides, two straps cross it, four anchors pin it, the broken lip fragments stand outside the cloth on the plate where the cover does not reach, and the worn track runs from the gate straight under it. Every one of those says a hole. What the default withholds is the DEPTH, which is precisely what a shroud withholds.
dna.was: did not exist. Nothing was promoted here and no shipped behaviour was touched. This is the cross-member argument the ten `warning` promotions left in registry notes, built as a body: nine of them describe their axis in terms of a doorway, a room, a distance and an approach, and not one of them contains any of those things.
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT THE YARD MAKES, and no member can make it, because it needs an approach.

Every one of the ten members is a body wearing a marking. A body carries its marking with it, so the question 'when did this reach me' cannot be asked of it — the answer is always 'when you could see the creature'. Put the same five markings on a plot of ground with a gate at one edge and a hole at the middle, and the five values sort themselves by WHERE THEY LIVE relative to the person crossing:

  stain   is on the ground you are walking on. To read it you look down, which is to look away from where you are going. It is also the only marking nobody chose to make.
  cage    is in the space between you and the hole. It works on your body, not on your judgement, and it works identically on the person who wanted to look in and the person who was going to fall in.
  beacon  is above everything and reaches the gate. It is the only value that puts NOTHING in the way — it informs and then leaves the decision with you, which is either the most respectful of the five or the most negligent, and the yard does not settle that.
  shroud  is over the hole and it is the only one that reaches you by REMOVING something. From the gate the yard reads flat and finished.
  none    is the control, and it is not nothing: an open pit in an open yard is completely legible as itself. Unmarked is not unknowable.

SO THE ROW TURNS. Ordered by how much a visitor at the gate can find out, it runs shroud (least) - stain - cage - none - beacon. Ordered by how much the yard has DONE about it, it runs none - stain - beacon - cage - shroud. Those two orders disagree at both ends: `none` is near the top of one and the bottom of the other, and `shroud` is the maximum of effort and the minimum of information. That is why the word needed five values rather than a slider, and it is invisible to any object that can only stand in one marking at a time — which is every member of the family.

ONE PIT, SOLVED ONCE. _solve() fills _g with the plate slabs, the pit depth, the track's length and midpoint, the two radii any marking may stand on, and the frame's own px-per-metre. Every builder reads out of it. No quantity in this file is computed twice, and the two rings were derived from the lip (PIT_HALF + 0.80 for the fence, PIT_HALF + 0.20 to PIT_HALF + 0.85 for the cloth) so that `cage` and `beacon` are seated at the same distance out and neither gets a nearer chair than the other.
dna.kin:
THE WORD AND ITS FIVE VALUES ARE TAKEN WHOLE, and not retyped. warning_yard.gd opens with `const WARNING_SOURCE := preload("res://commons/hazards/path_block/path_block.gd")` and validates against WARNING_SOURCE.WARNING_VALUES at runtime; every colour a marking is made of is read from the same file (WARN_STAIN_OUTER, WARN_STAIN_CORE, WARN_BAR, WARN_TAG, WARN_MAST, WARN_LAMP, WARN_CLOTH, WARN_STRAP). GDScript will not let an @export_enum hint be built from a constant, so the literal list is duplicated once as HINT_VALUES and _assert_vocabulary() push_errors at _ready if HINT_VALUES and WARNING_VALUES have drifted, or if the standing value is not in the family's list. The two cannot silently diverge, which is the science_screen fault closed by construction rather than by a gate run.

WHY path_block AND NOT kaleidocycle_enemy, which is where the builders were first written: path_block serves three of the ten tokens from one scene, its file contains the warning apparatus and nothing else, and it preloads a single shader — the other members are combat machines that would drag a dependency chain into a static diorama.

THE FAMILY IS NOT ONE VOCABULARY, and this was measured rather than assumed. Ten registry tokens declare `warning`. Nine declare [none, stain, cage, beacon, shroud]: path_cube, path_wedge, path_pyramid, kaleidocycle_enemy, kresling_spire, miura_crawler, scissor_stalker, cube_projectile_spawner, force_vortex. One — [[r_c]] — declares [beacon, stain, cage, none], which is REORDERED and one value SHORT. This yard builds the nine, and says why it did not build the four.

WHAT r_c's SHORT LIST COSTS, and it is not a style point. `shroud` is the value that breaks the scale: the other four sit somewhere on 'how much is said', and shroud says less than none while doing more than any of them. A four-value list without it reads as a monotone ladder from silent to loud, which is precisely the misreading the axis exists to prevent. r_c's own note is honest about its situation — 'at a resting pose beacon and none are identical by construction, which is the axis's own point, not a harness fault' — so the omission is a cube that cannot wear a tarp, not a disagreement about the word. It is still a hole in the census, and the yard's five bays are the argument that it should be filled.

AND THE ORDER MATTERS MORE THAN A STYLE POINT, for the reason retention_corridor found: build_dna_gallery trims value lists from the TAIL. Under the nine-member order the first value a capped sweep drops is `shroud` — the one that carries the argument. Under r_c's order it drops `none`, the control. Nine of the ten members are therefore one cap away from a sweep that quietly omits the point. This yard is not immune; it is declared in the majority order because it must be measurable against the nine, and this note is the flag.

THREE THINGS FOUND WHILE READING THE FAMILY, reported and NOT fixed here.
(1) path_block.gd's axis doc says the vocabulary was 'adopted word for word from [[catalyst_vent]]'. commons/hazards/catalyst_foe/catalyst_vent.gd contains the string 'warning' zero times. The credited ancestor does not carry the axis, so either the vent lost it or the lineage line is wrong; either way the family's own account of its origin does not check out.
(2) [[origami_droideka]] implements the whole apparatus — WARNING_VALUES, the export, five builders, the group, the teardown — and its registry entry at commons/artifacts/registry/hazards.json has no `dna` block at all. It is a working, reachable axis that no tool can see, which is the dna_specimen fault in mirror image: there the declaration existed and the code did not.
(3) The family's `hazard_warning` group is read by exactly seven files besides this one — path_block, kaleidocycle_enemy, kresling_spire, miura_crawler, scissor_stalker, origami_droideka and commons/primitives/cubes/CubeSpawner.gd — all of them members, and only ever to find their own dressing and free it. Nothing outside commons/hazards and commons/primitives touches it. Adopting it here is therefore safe and carries no gameplay meaning, which is what let this artifact keep the family's construction while being inert.

NO SECOND AXIS. `depth`, `hazard_kind` (pit / spill / live rail) and `approach` were all considered. Each would multiply the sweep and none would sharpen the claim: the yard's whole method is that the danger is held CONSTANT while the marking varies, and an axis that varies the danger is an argument that the marking depends on it — which is the opposite of what these five values show.
declines: THE retention_corridor MOVE — stand all five markings in the yard at once and vary something else. It was available (the five values sit SIDE BY SIDE, not nested: each names a different addressee and none contains the one before it, so unlike disclosure_cabinet's five, showing them together is not just the top value). It was refused because the yard would then measure a word the nine members do not measure, and the whole reason to reuse a family vocabulary is that the siblings can be compared. A synthesis whose axis nobody else declares is a new artifact with a borrowed name.

A DangerZone, a collider, a trigger volume or any damage at all. Refused on the brief's instruction and independently on the argument: a marking backed by a working trap stops being a picture of how markings work. It also would have made `shroud` a genuine trap for a player, which is a cruelty the artifact does not need to make its point and a maintenance hazard nobody asked for.

AN OmniLight3D AT THE BEACON. It is deterministic and it would have brightened a large area of the plate, buying a great deal of pixel difference cheaply. Refused twice over: a broad even brightening is exactly the change the critic's own subject_fraction note flags as suspect (frame and focus coming out equal is the tell that a difference is uniform), and a beacon whose evidence is that it lit the room is measuring the light, not the marking. Everything the beacon adds is geometry with an emissive material.

A SECOND MAST, A FLOODLIT APRON, OR ANY OTHER PADDING ON `beacon`. It is the thinnest value on this axis by a factor of two (see dna.predicted_degeneracy) and it was LEFT thin. A yard beacon is a mast, a lamp and a lit rim; the honest fixes to its thinness were already taken (the collar wraps the mast on all four faces instead of facing one way, the rim is 0.50 m rather than a hairline, and a stop bar crosses the track where the approach actually is), and going further would buy pixels by making the object less like the thing it is named after. This is the field_room ruling: if a value is thin because the thing it describes is thin, say so with numbers and leave it.

A HUMAN FIGURE for scale. The gate carries the scale instead — 1.85 m posts, 1.04 m clear — and it does it without adding a character, a rig, or a second thing for the eye to read. A figure would also have had to stand somewhere, and where it stood would have been an argument the axis did not make.

ANIMATING THE BEACON, or any flash, pulse, sway or reveal. The evidence is one still PNG per value; a rate and a duration are invisible to it, which is the info_board result. There is no _process and no _physics_process in the file at all, so a capture's settle cannot photograph this artifact half way through anything.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, from geometry, in changed pixels of a 760 x 760 tile. THE CLOSEST PAIR IS none <-> beacon, at 13,100 px = 2.27% of frame.

THE ARITHMETIC. dna.framing 0.60 on the union box puts the camera 21.063 m out, where the visible frame is 12.879 m across (165.87 m2 of screen area) at 59.01 px/m. The sweep's standpoint is yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, so the elevation is 14.90 degrees: anything lying on the ground is compressed by sin(14.90) = 0.2571 and anything standing up keeps cos(14.90) = 0.9664. Projected screen area added by each marking, summed element by element:

  beacon  mast 0.623 + collar (net) 0.135 + lamp (net) 0.403 + cap (net) 0.242 + two struts 0.408 + lit rim (7.00 m2 of ground x 0.2571) 1.800 + stop bar (1.60 x 0.36 m of ground) 0.148 = 3.758 m2 -> 2.27% -> 13,088 px
  stain   29.33 m2 of ground x 0.2571 = 7.542 m2 -> 4.55% -> 26,266 px. The 29.33 is a RASTERISED UNION of the six lobes, the four core bands and the two drag runs at 2.6 mm resolution, not a sum: the parts total 37.35 m2 and overlap by 8.02 (0.53 lobe-to-lobe, the rest lobe-to-core), and an earlier estimate of 29.0 by hand was 1.1% low.
  shroud  crown 2.972 + the two camera-facing skirts 3.003 and 2.368 + straps and anchors 0.30 = 8.644 m2 -> 5.21% -> 30,100 px
  cage    12 posts 2.790 + rails at two heights 2.561 + kick board 2.561 + 3 tags 0.457 + 4 braces 0.782 - overlap 0.30 = 8.851 m2 -> 5.34% -> 30,821 px

WHY BEACON AND NOT STAIN. Not because the ground is foreshortened — that hurts the stain, which is the runner-up — but because a mast is THIN. The beacon's whole standing structure is 0.22 m wide and its lit rim is a 0.50 m band; the stain covers 29 m2 of ground, the cage puts twelve posts and 13.25 m of rail run across the frame, and the shroud is a 3.4 m slab plus two skirts. The gap is 2.00x (13,000 against 25,963), which is wide enough that my soft numbers — the grey-level deltas — cannot close it. That is the falsifiable claim: BEACON CHANGES THE FEWEST PIXELS, by about half.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT, and what it would mean. If the sweep comes back with none <-> stain as the tightest pair instead, the cause is CONTRAST, not coverage: the beacon's material is emissive and half of it silhouettes against the dark backdrop above the plate's far edge, while every square metre of the stain sits on the lit plate. Expected focus for none <-> beacon is about 17% over the full tile (13,000 px x an estimated mean delta of 100 / (255 x 28,880 px in the hottest 5%)), and roughly 59% if the critic crops to the subject box — so 17% is the floor, above the WEAK threshold of 12% either way.

EVERY OTHER PAIR IS LARGER, structurally and not by luck: `none` adds nothing, so the four pairs involving it are exactly 'how much does this marking add', and the six marking-to-marking pairs are near-disjoint unions of two of the numbers above, the smallest of which (beacon <-> stain) is about 38,000 px. So the minimum is guaranteed to involve `none`, and it is `none` against whichever marking is smallest. Predicted mean focus across all ten pairs: about 40%. Predicted verdict: BITES.

NO PAIR IS PREDICTED TO BE IDENTICAL. Nothing here is occluded by anything else — the beacon stands at the pit's FAR corner from the camera, the cage ring is 0.80 m clear of the lip on all sides, the shroud never reaches the fence line, and the stain is flat. The one degeneracy that could occur is a fixture fault rather than a design one: if a sweep is run --staged, a 7.5 m floor-standing plot does not want a plinth under it and the pair AABB will grow. Measure unstaged.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL FIVE VALUES, not from the default. Union 7.50 x 3.89 x 7.50; diagonal sqrt(56.25 + 15.132 + 56.25) = 11.2974, radius 5.6487. The rig is dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) x PAD x framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 puts the camera at 5.6487 / 0.305731 x 1.9 = 35.11 m, where the visible frame is 21.46 m across and this 7.5 m plot spans 10.46 m of it — 49% of frame width, with the pit itself at 14%. PAD 1.9 already shows 1.9x the bounding-sphere radius, which is why a bench object wants framing well below 1.0.

AT 0.60 the camera comes to 21.063 m and the frame to 12.879 m. At the sweep's yaw of 0.62 the square plate projects 3.75 x (cos 0.62 + sin 0.62) x 2 = 10.462 m wide; with perspective (near corner at 20.219 m, far at 21.907 m) that is 0.2587 + 0.2388 = 0.4975 tan-units against the frame's 0.61146, or 81.4% OF FRAME WIDTH and about 40% of its height. The pit is 23% of frame width and the subject is roughly 17-22% of frame — well clear of the ~6% dilution floor and of the blank-render check.

IF THE DEFAULT'S OWN BOX HAD BEEN USED: `shroud` alone tops out at 2.049 m, giving radius 5.401 and a 33.57 m base distance, which at the same framing would seat the camera 0.9 m closer and hang the beacon's cap 23% above centre in its own tile. Framing off the default is how a value that adds height gets cropped in the one frame that needed it; the union is the only correct box and the code's Y max is the beacon's cap by construction.

GAUGE CHECK AT 59.01 px/m, because foresight_range shipped 0.028 m arrows onto an 18 m lane and sorting_hall drew a three-pixel gauge. Cage rail 0.10 m -> 5.7 px; cage post 0.15 m -> 12.3 px of silhouette; kick board 0.20 m -> 11.4 px; beacon mast 0.22 m -> 18.1 px; beacon lit rim 0.50 m of ground -> 7.6 px after the ground cosine; stain core band 0.75 m of ground -> 11.4 px (path_block's 0.16 m band scaled naively would have been 2.4 px, which is why it was widened); stain drag run 0.32 m -> 15.4 px; shroud strap 0.14 m -> 8.3 px; gate post 0.16 m -> 13.1 px with a 61 px opening. Every mark the axis is measured on is at least 5.7 px. The only sub-pixel-ish elements are the 0.03 m pit liners at 1.8 px, which are shading and carry no part of the axis.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED, and it is checkable rather than claimed. The file contains no randf, no randi, no randomize, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween, no physics body and no reference to the scene tree outside this artifact's own children. _ready is ungated and builds the entire plot plus its dressing standalone, so nothing has to be supplied for a still and the sweep's rescue path (apply_grid_config when the AABB measures zero) will never fire. The six lip fragments and the six stain lobes are fixed tables, not draws. Two captures of one value are two photographs of one object.

THE SWEEP SETS THE @export DIRECTLY BEFORE add_child, the grid sets config_warning metadata, and apply_grid_config takes a dictionary; all three land on the same _read_metadata_overrides, and apply_grid_config rebuilds ONLY the dressing and ONLY when the word actually changed and _ready has already built once. An unrecognised word keeps the standing value: a typo must never silently uncover a hazard, and it must never silently cover one either.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a thin number is read correctly.

CONSTANT AT EVERY VALUE, by construction and on purpose: the four plate slabs, the pit floor and its four liners, the six lip fragments, the worn track, and the gate with its lintel — 19 meshes and roughly 17% of the frame that cannot move. That is the control, and it is what makes the five tiles a comparison rather than five pictures. Anything that changes between tiles is a marking.

STRONGEST PAIRS, predicted from the geometry: `shroud` against `none` and against `stain`, because shroud is the only value that REMOVES the darkest thing in the frame — 3.0 x 3.0 m of near-black pit floor, 2.31 m2 of screen at a delta of about 180 grey levels — and replaces it with pale cloth. `cage` against `shroud` is the largest union of two markings.

WEAKEST PAIR: `none` against `beacon`, at 13,000 px. See dna.predicted_degeneracy for the arithmetic and for why it was not padded.

NO TEXT ANYWHERE. There is not one Label3D or TextScreen in this artifact, so LabelFramer has nothing to do, no plate is added behind anything, and no pixel of any tile is a rendered word naming its own value. Every pixel that differs between the five is geometry.

THE CAPTURE AABB IS THE REAL BODY and no `layers = 0` anchor is needed: every node in the file is a MeshInstance3D with a BoxMesh, there is no MultiMeshInstance3D and no CSG, so the mesh extent bounds the artifact exactly. The 7.5 m plate is also the widest thing in it at every value, which means the camera distance does not move between tiles for any reason other than the beacon's height — and that is already in the union box.

IF IT COMES BACK FAINT, check three things before the design. (1) Was the sweep run --staged? A 7.5 m plot on a plinth grows the pair AABB and shrinks every marking. (2) Did apply_grid_config get called with a `warning` key that is not in the list? An unknown word keeps the standing value by design, so five tiles of the default is what a typo looks like — run tools/check_dna_declarations.py --token=warning_yard first. (3) Is the standpoint doing the work? Four of the five markings live at or near the ground plane, which the canonical camera sees at 14.90 degrees; a probe from above would read them very differently, and per the standing gate an INERT verdict on this token is not reportable until tools/probe_anamorphic.py has been run on it.
